title: AstraNova inference stability & economics sprint review
summary: Quarterly checkpoint focused on usage patterns, cost anomalies from the last month, reliability incidents, and a short roadmap alignment. Agreed to a targeted pilot for KV-cache tuning and a Dedicated capacity trial for peak traffic windows.
next_steps: Redwood to share detailed cost breakdown spreadsheet by model and route (Maya) - due 2027-08-02
SE to run KV-cache profiling job and share results (Diego) - due 2027-08-06
Schedule 1-hour capacity-sizing call for Dedicated trial (Priya + Sana) - schedule by 2027-08-04
action_items: Maya Chen: send cost breakdown CSV and suggested savings levers - 2027-08-02
Diego Alvarez: run KV-cache latency profile and attach traces - 2027-08-06
Sana Mehta: provide peak window logs and QPS targets for week-of-2027-07-18 test - 2027-08-03
Rodolfo Vega: confirm compliance checklist items and which SOC2 artefacts are required - 2027-08-05
meeting_header: Date: 2027-07-28 15:00 PDT; Duration: 57m; Location: Zoom; Recording: yes; Notes: internal CSM+AE+SE from Redwood; customer leadership + infra leads present
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. We'll run through the usage and cost trends, hit the reliability incidents, then propose the KV-cache pilot and Dedicated trial. Quick round of intros?
[00:14] Liam (AstraNova): Liam here, head of platform. Sana's our infra lead and Rodolfo is SRE.
[00:20] Sana (AstraNova): Hi all.
[00:22] Diego (Redwood SE): Diego, I'm the solutions engineer on the account.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood CSM): Priya, customer success.
[00:30] Maya (Redwood): Cool. First slide — usage. Over the last 30 days you're up about 42% month-over-month in token volume, mostly driven by a new reranking route in production. We can see the bulk of the cost is that route and model selection.
[00:50] Liam: Yeah that reranker rolled out mid-June, we expected some lift but not quite this level. Latency's OK but cost bit us.
[01:02] Maya: Understood. We dug into the per-token breakdown; for reranking you're on a 13k context variant which is expensive. Two levers: reduce context or move to a quantized variant that still meets quality.
[01:20] Sana: Can you remind me which quantized variants you support? We tested q4 earlier and saw hallucination uptick.
[01:30] Diego: Right, q4 can change output quirks. We have a midline q5-style profile and also a hybrid that keeps float for attention layers. We'll share the profiles.
[01:44] Rodolfo: One thing we hit last week — a 6-hour tail SLO breach Friday morning. Service degraded around 03:12 UTC, traffic spiky and routing fallback sent requests to the smaller instance pool.
[02:00] Priya: We recorded the incident in the portal; Redwood trace IDs linked in the doc.
[02:06] Diego: I saw that — looks like autoscaler latency plus a KV cache cold miss storm. The runtime's continuous batching queued up and then eviction thrash caused token latencies to spike.
[02:22] Liam: Is that a runtime bug or config? We were on the default autoscale and cache TTLs.
[02:30] Diego: Mostly config and workload. The pattern was many short prefix hits — caching didn't help because prefixes rarely repeated. But our default batching window increased under load causing amplification.
[02:48] Sana: Would Dedicated capacity avoid that? If we had pinned pools would this be prevented?
[02:56] Maya: Dedicated gives predictable capacity and lets you tune autoscaling thresholds; it can reduce cross-tenant noise. But it doesn't magically fix cache miss patterns. For this incident we recommended three actions: KV-cache tuning, shorten batching window for that route, and a small Dedicated pilot for peak windows.
[03:14] Rodolfo: We like pilot approach. How long to get Dedicated test environment?
[03:20] Priya: Typically we can spin a pilot within 1-2 weeks once sizing inputs are provided. Diego will run a profiling job to give recommended pool sizes.
[03:30] Diego: I'll need your peak QPS and sequence length histogram for the route. If you can drop the logs in the shared folder I'll run the profiler.
[03:38] Liam: I'll drop a sample and the week-of-traffic we saw in July.
[03:42] Maya: On costs — we found two anomalies: (1) the reranker model used an older ver with higher per-token cost due to longer decode steps, (2) a misrouted internal test route that wasn't supposed to be at prod scale. Combined they explain ~27% of the excess.
[04:02] Sana: The test route was an internal job — that's on us, we'll gate it. The older model version is interesting; we thought we'd fixed it.
[04:12] Diego: We'll share the model-version audit. There might be a pin in config that kept traffic to the older variant.
[04:20] Maya: For immediate wins: switch reranker to the quantized hybrid profile for non-critical calls; implement a prefix cache TTL of 4 minutes and a reduced batching window for that route. That should reduce token costs by ~18% in our estimate.
[04:36] Rodolfo: Sounds sensible. Any risk to quality if we change the quantization?
[04:40] Diego: Slight risk — most of our internal evals showed negligible divergence on top-1 but some small delta on rare tokens. We recommend an A/B for 5% of traffic.
[04:54] Liam: We'll accept that.
[04:56] Maya: Security and compliance check: you asked for SOC2 artifacts and an audit log example. Priya, do you have the list?
[05:06] Priya: Yes, they want SOC2 Type II summary, SSO/SAML configuration notes, RBAC export, and KMS key rotation policy.
[05:16] Rodolfo: Also want more granular audit logs per-token for 90 days — is that feasible without massive storage cost?
[05:24] Maya: We can provide request/response audit logs and a sampling strategy; full per-token payload retention for 90 days is expensive but we can do metadata retention and sampled payloads. We'll include retention cost estimates in the spreadsheet.
[05:38] Sana: Good. Back to reliability: Diego, can you explain the KV-cache profiling you'll run?
[05:44] Diego: Sure. I'll run a replay of your traffic against a staging runtime with TTL and capacity variants. The profiler will emit p50/p95/p99 latencies, cache hit rates, and memory usage. Expect the report within 7 business days.
[05:58] Liam: If that shows improvements, what's the rollout plan?
[06:02] Maya: We'll do canary (2% traffic) then ramp 10/30/100% with metric guards on latency and quality. We'll use automatic fallback to the prior config if regressions are detected.
[06:14] Rodolfo: Good to have safety.
[06:18] Maya: A short note on cost modeling — we'll provide a delta sheet that ties into your internal cost center mapping so you can see net savings after Dedicated commit fees.
[06:30] Sana: How do commit discounts work for Dedicated? Is there a minimum?
[06:34] Priya: Standard is monthly or annual reserved capacity contracts. Discounts scale with committed throughput and term; we can model 3 scenarios in the cost sheet.
[06:46] Liam: On roadmap alignment — any upcoming runtime changes from Redwood we should expect that might affect our tuning?
[06:52] Diego: In August we plan a runtime kernel update that reduces memory for KV cache by ~12% on Ampere GPUs; it's backward compatible but we'll give a migration window.
[07:02] Maya: We'll flag that in the release notes and coordinate if you want to test it.
[07:08] Rodolfo: One last ops ask — can we get more granular route-level SLO reporting into our PagerDuty?
[07:14] Priya: Yes, we can map per-route SLOs to PD escalation policies; we'll need the SLO definitions from you.
[07:20] Liam: I'll send SLO targets.
[07:24] Maya: To recap — Diego runs profiling; Maya sends cost breakdown + model-audit; Priya schedules Dedicated sizing; customer provides logs and SLO targets. We agreed to a small Dedicated pilot for peak windows and an A/B for quantization.
[07:40] Rodolfo: Great. Anything else?
[07:42] Sana: Not from infra.
[07:44] Liam: Nope. Thanks everyone.
[07:46] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and profiler link.
[07:50] [00:00:00 end of recording]
